judgments.title: EXTRA EXCEL (MALAYSIA) SDN BHD v QUEK PECK KEOW
judgments.catchwords: Section 10(1) of the Arbitration Act 2005 - whether section 10(1) of the AA 2005 required the courts below to determine for themselves the existence and operability of the arbitration agreement, or whether that question ought to have been left to the arbitral tribunal under section 18 and the doctrine of kompetenz-kompetenz - whether the 2nd Stay Application and OS 2 are barred by res judicata or issue estoppel arising from the April 2022 Decision - the proper construction of Clause 1.3 in its November 2019 form, and in particular whether it ever entitled the Appellant to commence arbitration against its own distributor - whether the June 2021 amendment to Clause 1.3 could, consistently with ordinary contractual principles, be applied retrospectively to a dispute that had already crystallised and was already the subject of litigation - whether the Appellant had, in any event, taken a step in the proceedings within the meaning of section 10(1), disentitling it to a stay - whether Clause 1.3 is void, in whole or in part, under sections 24 and 29 of the Contracts Act 1950, because it caps the Respondent’s recoverable damages - whether the Appellant’s unilateral right to appoint the sole arbitrator renders the arbitration agreement void, or offends natural justice - whether the finding that the Appellant acted in bad faith was properly made without a trial.

names: LIEW HON KONG @ LIEW KWAN VOON

judgments.catchwords: Maple, the owner of an oil palm estate, appointed Solid Suncity as Property Manager by letters dated 15.11.2017 and 16.11.2017 on terms which included guaranteed fees of RM100,000.00 per month and an express stipulation that "the appointment is revocable in writing". Solid Suncity paid RM20,000.00 in February 2018 and nothing thereafter. Maple’s Liquidator terminated the appointment by letter dated 08.08.2025, without prejudice to Maple’s case that the arrangement was a sham, and applied under Order 14A of the Rules of Court 2012 for a determination that the agreement had been validly terminated and that Solid Suncity was liable to account. Held, allowing the application: the revocability clause is plain and permits revocation by written notice without cause; the material facts being admitted, the question was one of construction fit for summary determination. Proceeding without prejudice to the sham allegation is not approbation and reprobation. Res judicata does not arise, the earlier Suit 524 having been struck out without adjudication on the merits and having raised neither termination nor possession. The sham and conspiracy claims are reserved for trial. Solid Suncity was ordered to deliver up vacant possession and to render an account of the Estate within 30 days. Civil procedure – Order 14A of the Rules of Court 2012 – question of construction – material facts not in dispute – contract – revocability clause – termination without cause – material breach – approbation and reprobation – res judicata – striking out not a decision on the merits – company law – powers and duties of liquidator – recovery of vacant possession – account of profits

judgments.title: SIVACHANDRAN A/L S JAYARAJAH v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Review jurisdiction - Rule 137 of the Rules of the Federal Court 1995 -Inherent powers of Federal Court – All sentences passed to be in accordance with the law – Avoiding miscarriage of justice - Exceptional circumstances - Fresh evidence of prisoner’s death following whipping. Constitutional Law - Federal Constitution - Articles 5(1), 8(1) and 8(2) Fundamental liberties - Life and personal liberty - Human dignity - Equal protection of the law - Whether it is in violation of medical ethics for medical officer to be participate in the execution of whipping. Judicial whipping - Corporal punishment - Whether judicial whipping amounts to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment (“CIDT”) - Whether punishment of whipping is inconsistent with constitutional protection of life, dignity and bodily integrity. Whether whipping is disproportionate and therefore contrary to Article 8(1) - Whether exemption of women from whipping constitutes prohibited discrimination on ground only of gender is contrary to Art 8(2) - Intelligible differentia. Whether whipping is against Art. 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (“UDHR”) and the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration in its prohibitions against CIDT - Whether whipping is against customary international law.
